title: Baccalà alla Napoletana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Naples' version of salt cod, simmered in a bright tomato sauce with olives, capers, and pine nuts, a Christmas Eve tradition for families observing a meatless holiday meal.
longDesc: This preparation leans into Naples' love of bold, briny flavors — olives and capers cutting through the richness of the fish — and remains one of the most anticipated dishes on the traditional Neapolitan Christmas Eve table.
ingredients: 30 g (⅓ cup) raisins, soaked in warm water
80 ml (⅓ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt.
Drain, remove any skin and bones, and cut into large pieces.
Warm the olive oil in a heavy pan and sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the olives, capers, pine nuts, and drained raisins, and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Gently add the cod pieces and simmer for 15–18 minutes until the fish is tender.
Finish with fresh parsley and serve hot.
chefTips: Soaking the cod thoroughly and changing the water several times is essential to remove excess salt.
Handle the cod gently once added to the sauce, so it stays in recognizable pieces rather than breaking apart.
This dish is deliberately bold and briny — don't skimp on the olives and capers.
commonMistakes: Not soaking the cod long enough, resulting in an overly salty final dish.
Overcooking the fish, which causes it to fall apart completely into the sauce.
Using a thin, underseasoned sauce that doesn't stand up to the rich, briny cod.
servedWith: As part of the Christmas Eve Feast of Seven Fishes
healthBenefits: A good source of lean protein and calcium from the salt cod.
culturalNote: Baccalà alla Napoletana is a centerpiece of Naples' traditional Christmas Eve meatless feast, its bold, briny sauce a defining feature of the region's holiday table.
